utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. We are just having seen for the first time and I think Mr. Greaves mentioned something like that, the protection for a defence witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I mention there is no transcription coming up on the screens. My screen is blank. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I am sure the Prosecution has this application and it has no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we received it a couple of minutes ago. To the extent that the motion is requesting protection from the public or media of the identity of these people and that they be heard in private session, the Prosecution has no objection, but we just got it a few minutes ago. To the extent that there is other things, I am not sure they go to the Office of the Prosecutor. If they do, we have not had a chance to look at it, but I can say -- we can say we have no objection to them getting protection from the public or media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you notice at the last page, he has made certain requests that they be moved out of Vienna and transferred to preferably a German speaking area of Switzerland. Look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I believe that is a matter the Office of the Prosecutor takes no position on. I don't believe that it's within our purview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is there any urgency about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think the phrase used this morning by the Victim and Support Unit is time is getting on. We would like this as soon as possible, particularly bearing in mind the summer holidays are upon us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We will have to consult the Registrar also before we make any decision on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of course we understand that but, as we say, time is getting on and matters are becoming really rather more urgent than they have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We should be able to take it later in the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am very grateful to your Honours. I say that on behalf of my leading counsel and myself and I thank the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us get on with the day's proceedings. Who is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Mr Bart d'Hooge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How do you pronounce it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe we should ask the witness that. As you may have noticed, my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I found some difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I am not good with many different kinds of names, and I consider Flemish names among them. (Witness enters court) Mr Bart d'Hooge (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Take your seat.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Bart d'Hooge.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: How are you employed at the present time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am an investigator with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: By OTP do you mean Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Prior to working for the OTP how were you employed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was an investigator with the Belgian Criminal Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: How long were you an investigator with the Belgian police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For about ten years.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Have you been involved as part of your work within the OTP in investigation into crimes alleged to have been committed in the Celebici detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been working on the Celebici case since 1st September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: As part of the investigation did you participate in interviews of any accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Which accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I participated in the interview of Mr Mucic, Mr Landzo and Mr Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me start off with Mr Mucic. When was Mr Mucic interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr Mucic was interviewed in Vienna, if I remember well, in March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know when Mr Mucic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr Mucic was arrested in Vienna on 18th March.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Were you present when Mr Mucic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not present during the arrest, but I was in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did you yourself have any contact with Mr Mucic on the 18th, the day he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any contact with Mr Mucic on 19th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please describe what happened and how it was that you had contact with Mr Mucic and briefly just describe the surrounding circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interview took place in the building of the Ministry of Justice in Vienna in one of the rooms that were provided to us by the local authorities. I participated in the interview together with Mr Abribat, Mr Nicholson and our interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me go back for a minute. Where was it that you first saw Mr Mucic on 19th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We first saw him together with Dr Sada, a judge from the Vienna court, in an office.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. What occurred during this meeting? Was this the OTP interview or was something else going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was an interview done by Dr Sada about the extradition procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you or anyone else from the Office of the Prosecutor ask any questions or participate during this meeting with Dr Sada?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: What happened after the meeting with Dr Sada?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the meeting with Dr Sada we changed rooms. We went to another room.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Who is "we"? Who, in fact, went to the other room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The members of the OTP. Mr Mucic went away for a rest, I think. He took a rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Who showed you this other room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr Sada.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: After Dr Sada showed you this room, what did you do, you and the other members of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a very small room and we set up the audio equipment and video equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Mr Mucic came back. We talked briefly to him and then started the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. When you say you talked briefly to him, can you just tell us what -- can you give us the circumstances surrounding the brief talk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We wanted to explain Mr Mucic the way in which the OTP conducts an interview, meaning that we have to audio record, video record. We explain him the rights according to Rule 42 and 43, just technically how we do an interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Who conducted the interview on 19th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr Abribat.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. On 19th March did anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor other than Mr Abribat speak with Mr Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: At any time prior to or during the interview did Mr Mucic suggest that he might wish to have an attorney present when he spoke with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did anyone suggest to Mr Mucic for any reason that he should not have -- for any reason that he should not have an attorney?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, you've already stated that Mr Mucic was advised of his rights under the Tribunal Rules of Procedure. Are you aware of whether or not there is a recording of Mr Mucic being advised of his rights under Tribunal rules and procedures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did Mr Mucic indicate whether or not he was willing to give an interview and, if so, whether or not he wished an attorney to be present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he agreed to be interviewed and he didn't express his desire to have legal counsel present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was the interview of Mr Mucic completed on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did the interview then continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I continued on 20th and 21st March.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Going now to 20th and 21st, can you explain the procedure for those days that the interview -- the circumstances surrounding the subsequent portions of the interview on 20th and 21st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again at the start of the interview we advised Mr Mucic of his rights, asked him if he agreed to be interviewed with or without legal counsel and started the interview, took a break, continued after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. When Mr Mucic was advised of his rights on 20th and 21st, was that also recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everything was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was there a time, in fact, either on 20th or 21st, when an attorney appeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 20th March I think around the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Please describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we just finished the first part of the interview and proposed to have a lunch break, and an attorney appointed to him by the Austrian court, by the Vienna court, came into the room. I think his name was Dr Manfred or something. He told us that he was appointed by the court as the defence of Mr Mucic. He asked us if he could have a copy of the indictment and the rules of the Tribunal. Then he spoke briefly with his client in private.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he went away.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Did he say anything -- did the attorney say anything to you before he went away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He advised me that Mr Mucic said that he did not want a legal counsel present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. This occurred during a break; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: When the interview commenced again was there any notation or record made of the fact that -- reference made to the fact that this person had appeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot remember the exact words, but it should be somewhere in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. If you looked at a copy of the transcript would it refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. I would ask that the witness be given a copy of the exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit 101 for identification purposes. (Handed to witness). Sir, I'm going to ask that you direct your attention to page 33 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the third paragraph: "We would like to state, as required by Mr Mucic, defence counsel shall not be present at the questioning". This is, I think, what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. At any time on 20th or 21st did Mr Mucic ever -- I'm sorry. I already asked that. At this time -- excuse me. Can the witness keep that? Sir, I would ask you to also look at Prosecution Exhibit 101 and tell me if you recognise it and, if so, what it is, and then with the usher's assistance if something else could be given to the Registrar for marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the English transcript of the interview that we conducted in Vienna, and this is the transcript in Serbian, Bosnian, Croat versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Were you present at all times during 19th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And you yourself conducted the interviews on 20th and 21st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Have you reviewed the transcript of the interview of Mr Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Does it fairly and accurately reflect the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you are being shown what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution exhibit 101A and 101B, if I have the numbers correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is 101A and 101B.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, can you recognise what those are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are sealed envelopes with the original videotapes of the interview that was conducted in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution seeks to introduce Prosecution Exhibits 101, which is the transcript, 101A and 101B, which are the sealed tapes originals. I'm sorry. We have a technical issue before there is any objections. Just let me ask. We also have copies of the videos, an extra copy and it's really if the Registrar could instruct me whether or not they require that the envelopes be unsealed and, if so, whether or not they then would re-seal them, because we have them available, but if the originals are going to be unsealed, I understand that the Registrar may require that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Actually all the envelopes that we receive which are sealed are opened to verify the contents of the envelope. That was already the case with the exhibits in the case of Mr Delalic. The sealed envelopes that we have received were opened and then the exhibits were numbered. These were exhibits that all the parties received. When we receive copies of additional tapes, it's not necessary to put them in an envelope, nor to give them other numbers if they are copies of videos. They are simply given the letter C. The first envelope is A, the second B and this would be exhibit 101C.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Does the Registrar then reseal the envelopes or do they leave them unsealed once they've been marked?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We close them again, but we do not seal them, and then they are deposited under protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case I don't believe it's necessary to introduce the extra copies. At this time, your Honours, the Prosecution seeks to introduce exhibits 101, 101A and 101B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Tom Moran for Hazim Delic. First, I would ask that the court order any reference to Mr Delic in these be redacted for the reasons set forth both in my pre-trial memo and I believe I filed a specific memorandum of law on this. Basically I don't have the right to cross-examine Mr Mucic. I would ask at least until such time as he takes the stand that all references to Hazim Delic be removed from both the transcript and redacted from the tapes. I believe there is about fifteen references to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: That is not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How can you redact it? You can argue this should not be used as evidence against him as far as you are concerned. You can argue that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is my fall-back position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is what he is supposed to have said. This is on the record. Whether that can be used as evidence against you is a different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You cannot have redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Then I would object to them being used altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is not the purpose for which they are intended. They are intended for another issue. When the question of being used arises, it might depend on the purpose for which it was being intended, not Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I think it is Rule 8 where I have to object contemporaneously. Just in all caution I bring that to the court's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It will be a question of law whether the statement of one accused can be used as evidence against the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour. I am bringing it to the court's attention. That's why I am making the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I want to find out: these audio, videotapes, the initial ones, are they initialled by this witness or do they bear his signatures? I just want to find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, is it the case that these sealed envelopes bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My signature, the signature of a witness and the signature of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: On the tapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the envelopes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: On the envelopes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The envelopes were sealed by the Registrar you just told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Maybe I did not express myself well. Let me ask the witness. I think when I was referring to what the Registrar does, it was once we introduce them into evidence. It was not what had happened previously, who had sealed them previously. Let me just ask the witness. Sir, who sealed those envelopes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I sealed the envelope.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Who authenticated the tapes themselves?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask: what happened, sir to the originals of the videotape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't dispose in Austria of equipment to make a copy of the videotapes as set out in the rules, so we brought the videotapes -- we put them in an envelope, brought them back to The Hague, made a copy here and then went to the prison with the original tapes. We put them again in an envelope, showed them to Mr. Mucic and we sealed them and everybody signed on the envelope, because it's impossible to put the signature on the tape itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise your signature as being the signature you placed on the envelope at the time that the originals were placed in the envelope and sealed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I simply want to join Mr. Moran and at this point object to the use of any statements contained on these videos regarding my client, Mr. Landzo, as evidence in this case, just to have it on the record that I'm making the objection contemporaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Even if you did not, I think we observe the rules. Yes? Let's us hear you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I would like to join the objection of my learned colleague, Mr. Moran, that these tapes can (sic) be used against our client Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is that all you have for this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is a slight correction to the transcript. There is a slight correction to be made in the transcript. You said "cannot be used." The word is "can be used" in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Certainly the Prosecution will stipulate that Ms. Residovic is objecting to the use of this statement against her client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is no admission on your part. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have more for this witness. Has your Honour ruled on the admission of Prosecution's Exhibit 101, 101A and 101B? I do not know if there wants to be voir dire or we should continue with respect to other interviews. I'm at the court's pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You see why you have to speak slowly and clearly, precisely for these kind of reasons. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: With the record clearly reflecting that they've been admitted into evidence, I will now go, sir, with respect to Mr. Landzo. You indicated, sir, that you had participated in an interview of Mr. Landzo. Can you please tell us the date and the place and who was present other than members of the Office of the Prosecutor when Mr. Landzo was interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Landzo was interviewed by members of the OTP in the detention unit in Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Ms. Residovic, may I ask that you turn off your microphone. Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): I apologise. May I put a question? I did not hear the Ruling of the trial chamber that these documents have been accepted as evidence. After you there is the possibility of cross-examination and as far as I know only then can the evidence be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, what we've admitted are the tapes and the documents which have been authenticated even by the witness himself and the accused person. They have signed it and security was guaranteed, so I think they're admissible. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, if you would please continue, I believe you were telling us the date and place and who was present when Mr. Landzo was interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Landzo was interviewed by members of the OTP in the detention unit in Scheveningen, and I believe it was in July 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Who was present other than members of the Office of the Prosecutor and a translator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Defence counsel of Mr. Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Landzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Was Mr. Landzo also present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, was Mr. Landzo advised of his rights under Rules 42 and 43?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was the interview recorded and a transcript subsequently made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. With the usher's assistance I would now like to show the witness some exhibits. These have been previously provided to defence counsel. (Handed to witness). Maybe before anything is opened it can be shown to the witness, if that is possible. Those are just three extra copies for the court's convenience, Mr. Registrar. Sir, showing you what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution Exhibits 102, being the binder, and 102A, being the envelope, can you please tell us if you recognised what those are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a binder with the English transcript of the interview, the Serbo-Bosnian transcript and some of the exhibits used during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Have you reviewed the translation of the interview of Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Does it fairly and accurately reflect the interview taken of Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was that Prosecution Exhibit 102 that you just referred to, if you can look in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is number 102.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now directing your attention to Prosecution Exhibit 102A for identification purposes, can you please tell us if you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a sealed envelope with four tapes of the interview of Esad Landzo. It's marked on it 18th July 1996, detention unit, Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Are these the originals of the videotapes, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: When was this envelope -- is the envelope in a sealed condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's two sealed with two signatures on the envelope -- three signatures.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Those signatures are on the envelope?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My signature, Mr. Landzo and Mr. Brackovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Brackovic the defence counsel of Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution would seek to admit into evidence Prosecution exhibit 102 and 102A?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to conduct cross-examination for the purpose of establishing a foundation for objecting to the admission of these transcripts and videotapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You would when the evidence is given, because all he's now showing you are the secure tapes signed by the three of them, which is sought to be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, she is offering them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If the court admits them at this point, I am deprived of the opportunity of developing an objection and there's an objection that I can develop if I'm permitted to cross-examine at this point. I don't want to sit here silently and let them be admitted and then be told later that it is too late, they have been admitted and I did not make a proper objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know what objection you now have for the signed and sealed envelopes which contain those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, my objection will be they were not taken in accordance with the rules of this court. I can evenly establish that by cross-examining this witness. I cannot establish it by standing here giving evidence out of my own mouth, but I do not want to waive the opportunity to object to the admission of these. She has now offered them. She is asking you, the Prosecutor, to make a ruling now on whether or not they're admissible. I object to their admissibility, and I can show why they're not admissible if I'm permitted to do a cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can examine him as to whether the rules were complied with. Let us hear your cross-examination because I do not know what you want to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is a record prepared by him. Whether he has done it rightly or wrongly that can being argued in the light of your cross-examination. It may be a bit premature to cross-examine him at this stage. Your objection has been noted and come on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me tell you of my concern. It may be confusion between systems. At this stage in the courts I normally practice in if the court were to say on the record that these documents are admitted, then I am no longer able to contest their admissibility. They have been admitted. So in the courts that I practice in I have to lay the foundation for my objection and make that objection now or be forever barred. If that's not the case, I'm willing to wait until my normal turn in cross-examination and then show the court that there's a reason why they should not be considered by the court. Perhaps all that has happened at this point, if they've been marked and are now available in the event the court decides that they were properly taken, and if that is the case, then I'll wait until my turn. Now according to our rules, illegally obtained evidence can be removed at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: At any time. You see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I am sure it is so according to your own rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Even if a document has been admitted and later on it is found it has not been obtained in accordance with law, it can always be excluded from consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then I am at the court's pleasure. Would you prefer that I proceed now or wait until my normal turn of cross-examination at this witness? It is completely up to the court. I am happy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: All you need to do is show at any stage these documents were not obtained legally and the rules have not been followed. The moment you show that you bring yourself within the exclusionary rules of this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I fully understand that, your Honour. The only question is when would the court want me to do that, now or later in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Wait until the examination-in-chief is over. Your objection has come on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I would renew the same objections to exhibits 102 and 102A that I had on 101, 101A and B and C. I renew all those objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It is the same rule you apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand, your Honour. It is just a matter of making sure I do come within the contemporaneous objection Rule in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the same reasons Mr. Delalic makes the same objection to the use of these statements against him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It gives a much wider field. Even if a document has been admitted and it is found to be wrongly admitted, it can be excluded from consideration. That gives you a much wider scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I make the same proposition on behalf of Mr. Mucic? Can I also say this? I think the word "admitted" is perhaps an unfortunate word to use in the circumstances. I hate to refer always to one's own system. In England the word "produced" would be used. The Prosecution is asking the witness: "Do you now produce the tape or the transcript?" Perhaps that avoids confusion, because the word "admission" in legal terms can have a wide variety of meanings and can be misconstrued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually it's not the Prosecution which admits evidence. It's the Trial Chamber which does.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It is anticipated your Honours do that. So the process which my learned friend is, in fact, doing is inviting the witness to produce and place in the custody of the court the physical evidence. I hope that's a useful suggestion. It may not be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, going to Mr. Delic, you indicated previously that you participated in --the interviews which you participated in including those of Mr. Delic. Can you please tell us when Mr. Delic was interviewed, where and who was present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Delic was interviewed in the detention unit in Scheveningen. He was interviewed in the presence of his defence counsel and members of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Delic's defence counsel present on both occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Delic advised of his rights under the Tribunal Rules of Procedure, including Rules 42 and 43?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Were the interviews recorded and a transcript subsequently made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know why there were two interviews of Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Delic requested himself to be interviewed again, because if I believe -- if I'm correct, he wanted to make some corrections to his first interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. With the usher's assistance may I ask that certain proposed exhibits be shown to the witness? (Handed to witness). I would just ask that before any envelopes be unsealed that they be shown to the witness: I will note far for the record that copies of all these exhibits have previously been provided to defence counsel and three copies of Prosecution -- proposed Prosecution exhibit 103 are being provided to the court for its convenience. Sir, I'm asking you to look at what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution Exhibit 103. If you can please tell us if you recognise it and, if so, what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the English and Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian transcript of both of the interviews and exhibits used during the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Have you reviewed the transcripts of the interviews of Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Do the transcripts fairly and accurately reflect the interviews the Office of the Prosecutor took from Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do the transcripts accurately reflect that the Rules of the Tribunal, including that the accused was advised of his rights, were followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'm going to ask that you look at Prosecution -- what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution Exhibit 103A, and if you could please with respect to 103A tell us if you recognise it and, if so, what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. These are the videotapes, original videotapes of the interview with Hazim Delic conducted on 7th January. The second interview in the detention unit in Scheveningen, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when these tapes were placed in the sealed envelope and who witnessed their being placed in the sealed envelope?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was done immediately after the interview and it was done in the presence of the accused and his defence counsel. There's -- both their signatures are on the front said and also on the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My signature and the accused and the defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Directing your attention to what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution exhibit 103B, can you please tell us if you recognised that and, if so, what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four originally videotapes of the interview conducted on 19th July, also in the detention unit at Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. These are Mr. Delic's interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, first interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when those were sealed, in whose presence and whose signature appears on the envelopes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were sealed immediately after the interview. My signature is on the envelope as well as the accused and his defence counsel on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would seek to admit into evidence exhibits 102, 102A and 102B. The Prosecution has no objection if your Honours want to defer admitting them into evidence until after cross-examination. The court's indulgence. That concludes the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, to make sure that I understand the -- understood the court's ruling to Mr. Ackerman, if at any time in the future I can show that these -- that there was some problem with the admissibility of it, I can then move to exclude them from evidence, given that understanding of what the court's ruling was, at this point I will not raise any objections at all to their admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the Ruling and you can proceed to prosecution examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I assume, your Honours, that there will come a time, if not today, within the next day or two that the Prosecution will seek to play these videotapes in open court. I think Rule 78 requires that. We would certainly want to make sure that our objections are properly lodged before the tapes are played in open court, because I think they have to be played in open court under Rule 78. So I would want to make sure that my objections are properly lodged before the Prosecution seeks to have them played for the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you have made your objection and the Trial Chamber has noted the objections. Whenever the tapes are played, I think we will follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf of Mr. Delalic, I would like to renew our objection regarding the previous statements by the other co-accused, that none of their statements can be used against Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: A similar objection is made on behalf of Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Again, just so the record is clear, it is the Prosecution's position that under -- that the accused may not -- excuse me. Let me find the Rule. Under Rule 73 with the exception of Mr. Mucic on one issue, the accused may not challenge -- they may not seek the exclusion of these into evidence. I understand the court may have a different opinion, and I also -- if evidence later comes up suggesting -- raising new issues, the Prosecution, of course, reserves its right to call additional witnesses if necessary. Other than that -- I just wanted the record to be clear I'm not asking that the court do anything at this point. I would also, just so the record is clear, indicate that the Prosecution does not believe that it's necessary to play all the tapes in open court. Proceedings -- the Rule proceedings must be in open court but it does not mean, I believe, that every exhibit needs to be shown in its entirety. We will defer to the court. If the court wishes us to play the interviews in their entirety, we will do so. Otherwise we would just plan on introducing the videotapes into evidence, the transcript and then, if necessary, we will use some of it in closing argument, but unless your Honours direct us to, we were not intending really just for matters of time to play the interviews in their entirety but they are in evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Have you looked at Rule 95 as to the circumstances under which evidence could be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You have seen that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: That is an overriding provision for whatever might be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's right. I understand that, your Honour. The Prosecution also believes that Rule 73 is applicable, but I don't believe that this issue is going to come up because, of course, the Prosecution believes that these interviews were taken in full accordance with all protections, including the Tribunal's and any internationally accepted rights. So I was just for the record both noting our objection and noting that if additional issues were raised later, we may seek to call additional witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: One's apprehension is your submission that you only need to play a number of the tapes for the purposes of authenticating what has been claimed to have been done. At least you know that any aspect of it that has been challenged ought to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe -- I'm not sure I understand. To the extent I do, I do not disagree with your Honours. That is why the Prosecution try to bring witnesses to discuss in detail Mr. Mucic's challenge, because we know that those are challenges. With respect to the other accused, in particular Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic, in all frankness we do not know what the challenge is. So other than to have the witness state that the rules were complied with, we believe we've done everything we can, and if something later comes up such that the Prosecution believes it appropriate to bring more evidence to clarify an issue that the accused has raised, we will certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: So the limitation of the number of tapes you wish to show will depend largely on the challenges of the defence irrespective of the fact whether it has been admitted, because they might still challenge aspects of it which might not be consistent with the rules as a whole. They have been admitted for the purpose of evidence but the complete compliance with the rules as a whole might depend upon what has been shown on the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, your Honour, we are entirely at the court's pleasure. We believe that the witness has testified that the rules have been complied with, and we have admitted into evidence the transcript of the entire interview as well as the tapes, and we believe that they are admitted into evidence and that the Chamber may use them whenever they wish. We are certainly very willing to have the tapes shown in their entirety, if it's necessary, or for the defence or the Trial Chamber to look to certain portions of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What I wanted you to understand is that their admission is still subject to cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Certainly we have no objection to there being any cross-examination on any relevant issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I just mention one thing which is to do with the public nature of evidence? This is not an objection. It is merely something for discussion by your Honours. If the tapes are not played or the transcripts are not read out, the public at large will never know what the defendant said about these matters. It is an important aspect that all evidence be, as it were, subject to the closed session idea, heard in public. If your Honours simply take the tapes and transcripts away and read them privately, the people out there in the public gallery will never know what the evidence is and that is unfortunate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is your case that the transcripts do not accurately represent what has been said in the interview. For the public the transcript is all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am merely saying the public is not going to know what the evidence is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The transcripts are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: They are not being read out in public.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I believe, and the Registrar can correct me if I am wrong, all exhibits are public and so this evidence is available to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the witness is now open for cross-examination for anybody who wants to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is that the agreed order of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. The agreed order of cross-examination is, first, defendant Landzo; followed by defendant Mucic; followed by defendant Delic; followed by defendant Delalic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is Mr. d'Hooge, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Am I saying that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Why don't you correct me. I really want to try to say your name right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: D'Hooge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: D'Hooge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Close enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. d'Hooge, I don't have a lot of questions for you. I have a few. To the extent that those questions appropriately call for a "yes" or "no" answer, I'd appreciate that. In other words, what I'm saying is I'm not interested in you having -- in having you answer questions that I don't ask you. Do you understand what I'm getting to (witness nods) thank you. You shook your head "yes." Can we have a "yes" for the record please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I take it that English is not your native language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your native language is Flemish?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you speak any other languages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I speak French and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. What day was it that you told us that you went to the detention centre to do your interview of Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was 19th -- no, 18th July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: About what time did you go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That must have been around 9 o'clock. If you want to be sure, I can take a look at the transcript. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you go with anyone or did you go by yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went by car with the Tribunal car, with the members of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that would be who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The persons present during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That would be who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be myself, Ms. McHenry, the interpreter and Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the Prosecutor, Ms. McHenry, was present during the course of this interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And is therefore one of the witnesses as to what happened during the course of this interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you first arrived at the prison to conduct this interview, tell me where you first went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to the reception where one of the security guards came to pick us up and brought us to the detention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was Mr. Brackovic with you at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You don't remember where you met him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where did you go after you were picked up at the entrance to the prison by a security guard? Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the UN detention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Where in that detention unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think to the room where we conducted the interview. The recreation room, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is it a small room, large room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a large room.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was Mr. Brackovic there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was Mr. Landzo there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was anyone else there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Who brought the equipment that you used to do the audio and video of this interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We brought the equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "We" being you, Ms. McHenry and the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was Mr. McLeod present throughout this entire interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. McLeod was not present in the room where the interview was conducted but was in an adjoining room where the back-up material was placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What is the back-up material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe the video recorders, audio recorders, the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was he in a position where he could see what was going on during the interview or simply hear it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe he could hear and see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So he had a monitor there where he could monitor what was going on during the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His role is to monitor the sound and the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know where Mr. McLeod is from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. McLeod is from Scotland.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. McLeod speaks Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He doesn't speak it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You do not speak Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Ms. McHenry does not speak Serbo-Croatian to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The only representative there from the Office of the Prosecutor that spoke Serbo-Croatian was the interpreter or from the -- was the interpreter from the office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That was the only representative there that spoke Serbo-Croatian; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you mean representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's what you mean. Of course, you know that Mr. Landzo speaks Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Brackovic, of course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with how fluent Mr. Brackovic is in the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Prior to the time that this interview began did you hear or observe any conversation that took place between Ms. McHenry and Mr. Brackovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You can't remember whether there was such a conversation or -- is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You don't recall today seeing the two of them converse prior to the taking of this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall a private conversation that took place between Mr. Brackovic and Mr. Landzo in your presence or out of your presence prior to the taking of this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: After the very beginning of this statement, when you went through the process of advising Mr. Landzo of his rights, his rights to remain silent, his right to counsel, things of that nature, was there then a moment where Mr. Landzo and Mr. Brackovic had a conference out of your presence in order to make a decision whether or not to go forward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You cannot tell this Tribunal, I take it, that there was a time at the beginning of this statement where Mr. Brackovic in lieu of the warnings that had been given to his client had a conference with his client regarding the nature of what was about to take place, you have no knowledge about that, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If this did not happen during the recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you don't know that it happened at any other time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you have the exhibit which I think is 102 in front of you, the transcript? Could I ask the Registrar to give it to him, please? (Handed to witness). Now I think you have told us -- that is exhibit 102 that you are looking at now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think you told us that it contains both the English and the Serbo-Croatian transcript of the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to look at the Serbo-Croatian transcript of the interview and just tell us if you can read and understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. You have told the court that you have looked at this and it is a true and correct transcript of the interview that you conducted; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You, of course, could not make that determination with regard to the Serbo-Croatian transcript, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So when you told the court that you were referring only to the English transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell the court how you went about making the determination that it was a true and correct transcription of your interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I revised and checked the English transcript of this interview and qualified people from the translation unit checked both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, you told the court that you had done it, and I want to know exactly the process you went through in doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I do not understand or read Serbo-Croatian, I can't have done the Serbo-Croatian revision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you cannot tell the court, as you sit here today, from your own personal knowledge that the Serbo-Croatian transcript is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How did you make a determination that the English transcript is a true and correct reflection of that interview? How did you do that? Physically how did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I went through the transcript. I read it. I listened to the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you sit with the transcript and go through it word by word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Word by word, yes, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How long a time would that have taken you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now what, of course, you were listening to was the interpretation of the Serbo-Croatian into English and comparing that English interpretation with the English transcript; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Again, you were not able to interpret the Serbo-Croatian yourself to see if the English transcript is a correct interpretation of the Serbo-Croatian, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you look, please, at page 3 of that transcript? About one-third of the way down the transcript indicates that there is a statement made by someone identified as "I2". That would be you, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So in the transcript you are designated as "I2". That would be Investigator 2; correct? Ms. McHenry is indicated as Investigator 1, "I1"; correct? Was she at that time an investigator employed by the Tribunal rather than an attorney with the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Ms. McHenry is employed as an attorney.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Even though she is designated here as an investigator, she at that time also was an attorney; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is a detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The answer is yes. As far as you know, she was an attorney with the Prosecutor's office and not an investigator on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is correct, is it not, that in that paragraph that -- it is the second I2 paragraph on page 3 -- you make the following statement: "I have asked the interpreter not to interpret every single word, especially when we're speaking about background matters". Those are your words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now if I were, for instance, to say to you right now what time did that happen, I doubt that you would be able to give me an accurate answer to that question until I give you some background, that being what that means; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific about the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. If I were to simply ask you a question: "What time did that happen?" ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You see, that's the problem. You don't have any background. You don't know what I'm talking about, do you? Now if I tell you I'm referring to the beginning of this interview and then say to you: "What time did that happen?", I have given you the background that enables you to answer my question, haven't I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Although it's not very clear to me what you're pointing at.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You have asked the interpreter with this statement that I've referred to here on page 3 not to interpret background matters, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked her not to interpret every word when it referred to background.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your language was: " ... especially when we're speaking about background matters"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Because you do not understand Serbo-Croatian, you have no idea what it was the interpreter did not interpret to Mr. Landzo, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To me, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you would ask a question in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The interpreter would then interpret that question into Serbo-Croatian and ask it of Mr. Landzo. That's the way it worked, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the way it worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Because you don't know Serbo-Croatian, you have no idea what that interpreter left out of the question that was asked of Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think that she left any word out of the question. Maybe words out of the answer. That is the purpose of this sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it doesn't say that. It says not to interpret every single word, especially when speaking about background. That's what it says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It reflects the answer of the accused, not my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that there may be answers of Mr. Landzo that do not appear in this transcript because they were not interpreted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There might be some words out of the answer of Mr. Landzo that were not completely interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Because you don't speak Serbo-Croatian, you cannot tell this court, as you sit here today, whether the interpreter interpreted every word of your question, whether the interpreter interpreted every word of Mr. Landzo's answers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I repeat that the purpose of this sentence is to interpret every word of my question but not of the answer, because of the limited time. That is purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But it doesn't say that, does it? It doesn't say: "Interpret every word of my questions but leave out the answers." It doesn't say that there, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me this is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Read the part that says: "Interpret every word of my questions but be free about your interpretation of the answers." Just read that if it is clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I am going to object. I think the question has been asked and answered. The record speaks for itself. I think this is now argument rather than questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Actually you have made your point that he was trying to guide the interpreter to what she should say and what not to within the limits of what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: As long as the court understands my point, I'm satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's what you are trying to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What day and month did you begin this investigation, the Celebici investigation, did you begin working on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1st September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So by the time you took this statement you had been engaged in this investigation for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten months.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So in a ten month investigation when you are talking a statement from my client, perhaps one of the more important duties you performed in this case, your concern was to try to save time; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we only had one day to interview your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's true, is it not, that the only way that we can -- that the Tribunal can know and that we can know for certain what was left out of either questions or answers in terms of the interpretation is to have the interpreter go through the tapes and make that determination? Because you don't know Serbo-Croatian, you could not do that, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not do it. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Any other cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I say this? I am in a bit of a quandary. I had filed earlier in this case a motion to permit me to file a challenge to this statement in accordance with the rules for that challenge to be filed late, and therefore to let me go into a complete presentation in an effort to try to suppress the statement. You will recall that I argued that in front of this court several days ago, my contention being that Mr. Brackovic was insufficiently familiar with Anglo-American jurisprudence and therefore did not and could not have given his client proper advice. Although it was made fairly clear to me from the bench when I made the argument what this court's ruling is going to be, the matter was taken under advisement and I was advised that there would be a ruling later on. That ruling has not yet been made so I still don't know if I am permitted to go forward with that matter, but in any event it would be done with different witnesses. I think that would complete my cross-examination of this witness in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually what you sought to do then was to bring an application out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Outside the period. That is what was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Exactly. All I am saying is it has not been formally rejected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: No, it has been. The Ruling has been but apart from a more considered version not having been circulated but it was ruled you cannot be allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That is fine. I certainly had that sense at least.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I think I am in the same boat that Mr. Ackerman is in; is that correct? I made a similar application and although the written decision isn't out, that it has been overruled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, on the same basis we indicated that you could not bring that application at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That's fine, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Because -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that I understood the court's Ruling. I would not argue with the court over its Ruling. I just wanted to -- unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Olujic, you have something to say? MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): My name is Zeljko Olujic, Mr. d'Hooge. I am defence counsel of Mr. Zdravko Mucic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just want to add something. A few minutes ago I asked permission of the court to add something to my testimony. Is it possible that I do it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think he is asking to answer a question of mine which I'm convinced he has already answered. If the Prosecution wants to ask him additional questions on re-examination, that's their business, but I don't think it is anticipate the business of the witness to begin volunteering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually you've closed your case and the cross-examination has ended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Thank you. Mr. d'Hooge, am I pronouncing your name properly? Mr. d'Hooge? I consider you to be a highly qualified person, a highly qualified witness. You are a policeman coming from Belgium. You have considerable experience of ten years in the service. Could you tell us, please, whether you graduated from the police academy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Did you study at the police academy any law subject such as the criminal procedure law of Belgium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not only at the police academy but also at university.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Which? The school of law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And criminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: That's very fine. Tell us, Mr. d'Hooge, according to the Belgium law on criminal procedure with respect to arrest do you know how long a person can be kept in detention before a decision is taken by the investigating judge, how long that person may be held by the police?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I object, your Honour, as to the relevancy of Belgian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: All I'm asking is this, your Honours, to lead up to the procedure which took place in Austria and it has to do with my client who had to be treated according to the laws of Austria and the Republic of Croatia, and considering the witness is a qualified person, I'm asking how these matters are regulated in his country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can put your question and he can answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You should answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to explain, although I don't think this is the correct place, but we have a totally different legal system than the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Counsel just wants to know. Answer his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the police, we can keep a suspect for 24 hours before he is interviewed by a judge. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Thank you. You travelled to Austria, to Vienna. Do you know how this is regulated by the law on criminal procedure of Austria, since you were going to Austria; in other words, how long a suspect may be held by the police before he is interviewed by the judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the Austrian system.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Could you tell us, Mr. d'Hooge -- let us reconstruct the events of 20th March 1996. At 9.30 you interviewed Mr. Mucic. Does that correspond to the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I have a look at the transcript, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Will you please provide the witness with the transcript? (Handed to witness).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the transcript of the ... I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Fine. On that occasion did you ask Mr. Mucic -- did you advise him that he is entitled to an attorney of his choice, and if he cannot find him then one would be assigned to him, and then did you go on to say -- to ask him whether he agreed to be interviewed without the presence of an attorney? So will you check, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Then you told him that he was entitled to an interpreter free of charge, an attorney free of charge and an interpreter free of charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness nods).

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, in connection with the previous question for the benefit of the record, the transcript, will you please give us your answer in words, "yes" or "no." So you asked Mr. Mucic or rather you mentioned to him in addition to a defence attorney that he was also entitled to an interpreter. Isn't that so. You nodded "yes", but will you say "yes"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. d'Hooge, when you were in Vienna how many times did you ask Mr. Mucic whether he agreed to be interviewed without an attorney, if you remember, of course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember. I should inspect the transcript, the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: You don't remember, therefore? You can't recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber will rise for 30 minutes and you will come back with your cross-examination. (11.30 am) (Short break) (12.05 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHITE
utterances.text: I apologise for our few minutes lateness. We were having a discussion. Can we invite the witness now? Invite the witness. (Witness re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly warn him he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I should like to remind you that you are still testifying under oath. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can. MR. OLUJIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Mr. d'Hooge, let us complete this section regarding the events on 20th March 1996. You were conducting the interview with Mr. Mucic, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, Mr. d'Hooge, in addition to that interview and the meeting with Mr. Mucic in Vienna, after Vienna did you have occasion to talk to Mr. Mucic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
